look_here_first: LOOK FOR THE NEEDLE-LIKE LEAVES AND HAIRY FRUIT FIRST. Beetle spurge (Euphorbia eriantha) is an UPRIGHT or ascending desert spurge, not a creeping sandmat. Most main-stem leaves are ALTERNATE, linear or narrowly elliptic (20–55 × 1–3 mm) with only 2–4 tiny teeth near the tip. At the flowering ends, 2–3 linear green BRACTS are opposite or whorled; don't mistakenly call all stem foliage opposite. The fruit is surprisingly conspicuous: an oblong, commonly white-HAIRY 3-lobed capsule 4.4–4.9 mm long, often green/white mottled (photographed clearly). Tiny cyathia are clustered among fruits, with gland appendages described by Flora of North America as WHITISH, densely hairy, divided into 5–12 narrow fringes and curled INWARD over the glands; our existing photos show the hairy flowering clusters, but not individual inward-turning hairs/fringes with certainty. Compare E. exstipulata: usually conspicuous leaf teeth and white/pink appendages that do NOT fold over the gland. Genuine mature seeds are 2.8–4.1 mm, pitted/warty and carry a caruncle; do NOT point to a striped green CAPSULE and call it a seed. FNA western-desert ecology is not evidence of Hays County nativity; native-range review remains paused.
photo_note: FIVE physically reviewed exact-species source JPEGs with THIRTEEN verified visible-structure arrows (Eric Knight CC BY; obatalov, debm, creamnosugar, yamstress photo-specific CC BY-NC). They teach slender leaves, narrow green upper bracts, hairy cyathial group, conspicuously larger striped hairy CAPSULES, and desert branching habit. Original source pixels checked 2026-10-21. Two diagnostic images still need independent licensed macro evidence: the precise 5–12 hairy gland-appendage fingers curved INWARD over the glands, and actual mature separated pitted/knobby seed with visible caruncle and 1-mm scale. Southwestern Arizona Flora Figure 26 has a seed plate, but the plate is a REFERENCE LINK only because its public website redistribution license is not established. No substitute image from another species will be used.

learner_visual_status.note: Five real checked licensed photographs teach alternate long narrow main stem leaves, opposite/whorled green terminal bracts, small woolly cyathia and conspicuously larger mottled woolly fruits. FNA's diagnostic folded fringed gland hood and mature carunculate seed remain photo holds.

taxonomic_note: Euphorbia eriantha Benth. is accepted in POWO. Distinct from creeping, opposite-leaved Euphorbia sect. Anisophyllum: this is an ascending desert Euphorbia in sect. Poinsettia, with alternate lower/midstem leaves, narrow green bracts and uniquely hairy, strongly incurved fringe-like gland appendages. State native TX; target county status remains unreviewed.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Euphorbiaceae, Euphorbia sect. Poinsettia (subsect. Erianthae). Cyathia are tiny cup-like reproductive units, not ordinary true-petaled flowers; fruit is a capsular spurge.
morphology_keys.habit: Annual or short-lived perennial with taproot; erect to ascending 10–75 cm; curving branches. Rocky desert washes and slopes, not a presumed common Hays County species.
morphology_keys.leaves: Main stem leaves ALTERNATE (basal node may appear opposite), 20–55 × 1–3 mm linear to narrow linear-elliptic with pronounced midvein; 2–4 tiny teeth close to the apex or practically entire to naked eye. Lower face sometimes short soft hairs; upper face often nearly glabrous.
morphology_keys.bracts: Upper flowering bracts 2–3, OPPOSITE or WHORLED, linear green and leaf-like, subtending terminal few-cyathium branches; distinguish these from the actual alternate main stem leaves.
morphology_keys.cyathia: Terminal cymose group, tiny hairs cover the involucre; 2–5 commonly 4–5 green-maroon shallowly cupped glands, 0.5–0.6 mm wide, commonly hidden by WHITE/gray dense hairy appendages folded inward over glands.
morphology_keys.gland_appendages: Extraordinary whitish hood-like appendages 0.5–1 mm, cut into 5–12 long fine subulate fingers, densely whitish-hairy, CURLING OVER glands, vs E. exstipulata appendages that do not cover glands.
morphology_keys.ovary_capsules: Oblong-ovoid approx 4.4–4.9 × 3.5–4.1 mm 3-lobed fruit, canescent (covered in short white/gray hairs) with sometimes hairless patches; much larger and hairier than a tiny sandmat's fruit.
morphology_keys.seeds: Mature true seeds oblong or ovoid, 2.8–4.1 × 2–2.4 mm, mottled black and gray or light brown, flattened dorsiventrally, coarsely tuberculate/pitted, with an obvious pale caruncle at attachment end. Do not confuse developing capsule patterns with detached seed surfaces.
best_field_traits: ALTERNATE, linear near-needlelike 2–5.5 cm × 1–3 mm leaves
Upper opposite/whorled GREEN leaf-like flowering bracts (not showy white bracts)
Tiny almost concealed terminal cyathia with HAIRY white appendages folded inward over glands
Large white-gray hairy, often mottled oblong 3-lobed capsules
Mature large 2.8–4.1mm visibly warted/mottled seeds with caruncle
Generally erect or ascending instead of creeping sandmat

comparisons.key_distinctions: Use alternate very narrow whole-green main-stem leaves and very hairy, oblong 4.4–4.9 mm fruit to recognize E. eriantha. To separate the closest E. exstipulata: inspect visibly more toothed leaves and gland appendages that remain OUTWARD / not curled over its glands, versus eriantha densely hairy hood fringes that curve inward and obscure its glands; actual micro comparative photos not yet available. E. heterophylla has broader variable leaves and smooth capsules, E. cyathophora showier bracts; E. bicolor and E. marginata conspicuous white-bordered terminal bracts. No false Hays county native status.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: BEETLE SPURGE — NEEDLE LEAVES, WOOLLY FRUIT, HIDDEN GLANDS
steps: Photograph a full erect/ascending plant, then trace middle STEM nodes: foliage is ALTERNATE. Two or three opposite/whorled leaflike parts higher up are reproductive BRACTS, not proof that all leaves are opposite.
Under a ruler check main leaves 20–55 mm long and only 1–3 mm wide; they often appear entire, with 2–4 tiny teeth near their tips.

On a terminal branch compare the LARGE elongated 4.4–4.9 mm WOOLLY 3-lobed CAPSULES against the much smaller white-hairy cyathial units. Our first two actual photographs show this size difference clearly.
At 20–30× isolate ONE cyathium: photograph a white hairy hood with 5–12 fine, inward-curved fringe segments lying over an actual gland; this remains a high-priority true diagnostic photo gap.

Find only a naturally released mature seed where permitted: check a distinct mottled, tuberculate/pitted seed with visible PALE CARUNCLE (2.8–4.1 mm according to Flora of North America). Do not call a striped hairy fruit a seed.

Compare E. exstipulata: more obviously toothed leaves; its white/pink gland appendages may be fringed but are not incurved across and hiding the glands. E. heterophylla has much broader leaves and glabrous fruit.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Current 13 photographic arrows resolve the coarse, highly recognizable characters only. The exact 5–12 curled fringes and actual ripe seed still lack independently rights-cleared images. This is western desert field-ID reference, not verified Hays native flora.
